title: Sharp and broad harmonic source responses differ by 7 to 9 arcsec in two TESS sectors of TIC 134197519
abstract: We test source-location consistency in the selected best sectors of 126 on-target complex periodic variables. We fit public TESS SAP flux and centroid first moments in broad and sharp harmonic bands. The median response difference is 0.415 arcsec; 120 objects have a nominal per-object 95% upper radius below 5 arcsec. One new candidate, TIC 134197519, has differences of 8.99 and 7.44 arcsec in sectors 61 and 88 after pipeline position terms are fitted. Both halves of sector 61 agree. Full-waveform target offsets are only 3.48 and 2.18 arcsec. An exact coefficient identity and synthetic test show how broad modulation can hide an offset sharp signal. The sharp sky response changes between sectors and does not identify a fixed neighbour. The result flags a source-location problem; it does not establish a blend or change the population rate. Fixed image-response assumptions, aperture and background effects, source selection and conditional error estimates limit inference. Original code, aggregate evidence, input hashes and separate-scratch repeat steps are included. External record tables and FITS files are excluded.

display.caption: Position-adjusted broad, sharp and full source responses for TIC 134197519. The sharp response differs from the broad response in both sectors, but does not give a stable sky position. The circle has radius 5 arcsec.
Distances between sharp and broad harmonic source responses in the selected best sectors. The dotted line is 5 arcsec. These are relative responses, not distances from the named target.

citations.reason: Uses the selected targets, periods and best-sector filenames to audit whether broad and sharp morphology give consistent centroid source responses.
Prior frequency-specific localization of variability in TESS images. The present audit uses flux moments rather than per-pixel PRF fits.
